title: Calibration Run Governance & Validation Hub for FP8/INT8 Profiles
creator: Amit Patel
description:
Goal: Create a centralized Calibration Run Governance and Validation Hub in the Redwood Console to manage FP8/INT8 quantization profile calibration jobs, their artifacts, retention lifecycle, and access controls. The hub should make it easy to run calibrations, review accuracy regressions, approve production-ready quant profiles, and maintain an auditable lineage for compliance and reproducibility.

Scope: UI and API surface for creating calibration runs, scheduling/running jobs (one-off and recurring), storing calibration artifacts (calibration logs, statistical histograms, profile artifacts, validation datasets, eval reports), retention policies, RBAC controls for who can start/abort/approve runs, and validation gating for automatic or manual promotion of quant profiles. Support both FP8 and INT8 calibration flows and a shared accuracy validation pipeline that ties to Redwood Optimize evaluation datasets and thresholds.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: building new quantization kernel implementations, low-level runtime quantization engine changes, or extensive changes to model compilation pipeline. Those will be separate ENG tickets and linked as dependencies.

Key deliverables: 1) Console UI flow for run creation, run list, run detail, artifact browser and approval workflow; 2) Backend job orchestration endpoints and scheduler integration for retries, concurrency limits and resource tagging; 3) Artifact storage schema and S3 prefix conventions with lifecycle rules and soft-delete/archival; 4) RBAC mappings and new privilege scopes (calibration.create, calibration.approve, calibration.view, calibration.delete); 5) Accuracy validation pipeline integration: threshold config, diffing against baseline, and pass/fail gating; 6) Audit events and run lineage metadata surfaced in Console and exported to customer logs.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Users can create FP8 or INT8 calibration runs via Console and the public API with config: model, dataset, quant profile baseline, target latency/cost constraints, and validation thresholds.
2) Each run produces a stable artifact bundle (profile artifact, histogram dumps, eval report with metrics) stored under a deterministic S3 prefix and visible in the Console run detail page.
3) Retention settings allow org-level defaults and per-run overrides; artifacts older than retention are either soft-deleted or archived according to policy and marked in run metadata.
4) RBAC: only users with calibration.create can start runs; calibration.approve is required to mark a profile as production-ready; calibration.view can see artifacts; calibration.delete can remove artifact bundles.
5) Accuracy validation pipeline computes metric deltas vs baseline and marks run as PASS/FAIL; failing runs are flagged and optionally trigger a rollback or notify owners.
6) Audit logs contain user, timestamp, action (create/run/approve/delete), and run UUID.
7) API contract documented in Console API docs and integration tests cover run lifecycle: create -> run -> artifact availability -> validation -> approve/decline -> retention purge.
implementation_notes:
Backend: add /calibration-runs v1 endpoints (POST /calibration-runs, GET /calibration-runs/{id}, POST /calibration-runs/{id}/approve, DELETE /calibration-runs/{id}) and a scheduler worker that enqueues jobs onto existing GPU job queue with tags for quant-type (FP8/INT8), priority and dataset. Reuse existing runtime executor but add a thin orchestration layer to capture artifacts and KV keys.

Artifact storage: use S3 prefix pattern: s3://redwood-calibration/{org_id}/{project}/{model_id}/{run_id}/{artifact_type}/{filename}. Maintain a run_manifest.json at run root capturing parameters, git commit for model, dataset snapshot id, and validation summary. Lifecycle rules managed via object tagging: retention-days and archival-phase. Provide a console action to trigger immediate archival or permanent delete (permission gated).

RBAC: introduce new scopes in IAM service and wire Console role editor to expose checkboxes for calibration scopes. Default workspace admins have all scopes. Team leads can be granted calibration.approve. Map to internal policy names: calibration:create, calibration:approve, calibration:view, calibration:delete.

Validation: integrate with Redwood Optimize eval harness — create a validation job that runs eval sets in isolated environment and computes metrics (accuracy, EM, ROUGE depending on eval). Output standardized report JSON with metric_baseline, metric_run, delta, and verdict. Allow threshold config per metric in run creation.

UI: Run list should support filters (model, quant-type, status, owner, date) and a compact summary of validation outcome. Run detail shows artifact browser, timeline (queued, running, completed), logs link, evaluation diff visualization and approve/decline button. Add a small badge to model page indicating 'has approved INT8 profile vX' with link to promoter run.
tasks: Design Console screens: run creation, run detail, artifacts browser (DES-1298)
Artifact lifecycle automation and S3 tagging rules (ENG-7241)
IAM scopes and Console role editor changes (ENG-7450)
Integrate Optimize eval harness and validation job (ENG-7623)
E2E tests: run lifecycle and retention purge (ENG-7922)
Docs: API docs and run governance playbook (PM-9130)
risks: Artifact storage costs if retention defaults are too long
Incorrect validation thresholds could block safe profiles or allow regressions
RBAC misconfiguration could permit unauthorized approvals
Runtime failures expose sensitive model telemetry in logs — ensure log scrubbing
open_questions: Should we support multi-run composite validations (ensemble of datasets) in v1?
Do we expose maintenance 'purge' to org admins or only to Platform SRE?
How long should soft-delete window be before permanent deletion? 7, 30, or 90 days?

acceptance_test_plan: 1) Create FP8 and INT8 runs using Console and API. 2) Confirm job executes on runner and artifacts appear under s3 prefix with expected manifest. 3) Run validation with intentionally lowered thresholds to force FAIL and verify alerts + block on approve. 4) Grant calibration.approve to a test user and verify approve flow promotes profile and exposes badge on model page. 5) Set retention to 7 days for a test run, simulate clock forward and ensure soft-delete / archival marks object and clears from Console after purge window. 6) Check audit log entries for each action and ensure KMS encryption and object tagging applied.
